PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: Airloom is proposing to deploy a novel wind energy technology in a small  temporary  non-commercial pilot project. The Project consists of an elevated track system with reticulating wings that travel along the steel track system. The total area required for the system will be similar to a high school running track  or approximately 5 acres.  \r\n\r\nThe height of the project will be 20-meters (65-feet). The system is expected to have approximately 28 individual  20-meter (65-foot) tall  supports holding the track at a 20-meter (65-foot) track height  with each support having its own foundation. The 530-meter (1 740-foot) long steel track will hold 27 wings. Given the temporary nature of the project  it will not interconnect to the grid to deliver power  and there will be no new construction of overhead transmission or substation facilities. In addition to the track system  the project will include internal access roads  a temporary construction/staging area  a mobile construction trailer/office  a backup generator  an electrical collection system  a supervisory controls and data acquisition system (SCADA)  and at least two 40 -meter meteorological towers (reported as the tallest/total structure height)  and load banks to safety dissipate energy generated by the device. The project will not transmit any frequencies.  The project will be decommissioned and fully dismantled following the approximately 24-month operational period.

County  Wyoming.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: Eurus Energy America LLC (Applicant) plans to construct a temporary meteorological tower (met tower) in Polk County  Oregon to collect wind resource data (Project). This data will be used to evaluate the potential development of a wind energy facility in the region. The mast will consist of an approximately 196.85 foot (60 meters) tall tower and will be supported by a series of wires  anchored to the ground in four directions. The temporary met tower is proposed to be in operation for 1-3 years  in which it will then be decommissioned. A broad construction window is provided  however  met tower installation is estimated to take 3 days.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The Project is located in Grand Ronde  Oregon  south of State Highway 18 between Grande Ronde and Boyer  northwest of Rock Creek  east of Salmon River. The site is located on a dirt road that forks off of the OR-18 W. Once at the top of the bald hilltop  the dirt road forks off again to the right and the site is at the top of the bald hilltop. The base of the tower is East  approximately 200ft away from the dirt road. There are no trees at the top of the bald hilltop.
